issues.description: The solution treats the symbol display_start inconsistently: main computes the pixel address by loading the symbol's address (mov esi, display_start) but set_pixel uses the memory at that symbol (add eax, [display_start]) — i.e. it dereferences display_start instead of using its address. The problem statement and template treat display_start as the start address of the frame buffer. Using [display_start] reads/writes the buffer contents as a pointer value (and is likely zero/uninitialized), which will produce incorrect absolute addresses and invalid memory accesses. This mismatch between correct address usage in main and incorrect dereferencing in set_pixel is a structural bug in the solution and will confuse students about how to use the display_start symbol.
issues.suggestedFix: Treat display_start consistently as the base address (not its contents). In set_pixel replace add eax, [display_start] with add eax, display_start (or compute the address into a register via mov/lea, e.g. mov esi, display_start; add esi, eax; mov [esi], ecx). Ensure all occurrences use the symbol as an address so the computed offset is added to the buffer base address.
